answers.explanation: Adding water dissolves the salts and filtration removes the sand; sublimation then drives off the ammonium chloride.
A pure crystalline solid melts sharply over a narrow temperature range, while impurities broaden the range.
Equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, so 50 cm3 of ammonia matches 50 cm3 of nitrogen.
8 g CH4 is 0.5 mol, and 22 g of propane (CH3CH2CH3) is also 0.5 mol, so both occupy 11.2 dm3 at s.t.p.
Doubling both V and P requires T to be multiplied by 4, so T = 4 x 273 = 1092 K.
Relative molecular mass equals twice the vapour density, so Y is the vapour density of the gas.
Rate ratio = square root of (density of Y / density of X) = square root of (2.0/0.5) = 2.
Higher temperature increases molecular speed, so molecules strike the container walls more frequently, raising the pressure.
Ammonia has four electron pairs around nitrogen arranged tetrahedrally, with one lone pair giving a pyramidal molecular shape.
Silicon (atomic number 14) has electronic configuration 2,8,4, so its valence shell holds 4 electrons.
Electronegativity decreases down a group because the bonding pair lies farther from the nucleus as atomic size increases.
The diagram shows three shells with two electrons in the outer shell, which matches magnesium (2,8,2).
X (group 1) and Z (group 7) form an ionic XZ, while Y (group 5) and Z form a covalent YZ3.
Deuterium has one proton, one neutron and one electron, so it is an isotope of hydrogen with mass number 2.
Anhydrous calcium chloride absorbs water vapour, so the change in mass of the drying tube measures the water vapour in the air.
A deliquescent solid absorbs enough atmospheric moisture to dissolve and form an aqueous solution.
Oil on coastal water blocks oxygen and sunlight, which destroys marine life.
Sodium chloride is so highly soluble that no saturated solution forms with a measurable ion product, so no solubility product is defined.
Moles of KNO3 = 20.2/101 = 0.20 mol in 100 g (about 0.1 dm3) of water, giving 2.00 mol per dm3.
Adding a concentrated acid to a solution at pH 3.4 increases the hydrogen ion concentration, so the pH falls below 3.4.
Calcium oxide is a basic oxide that reacts with acids and dissolves to form a base, so it is a base.
Moles of ethanoic acid = 0.020 x 2.0 = 0.040 mol, giving 0.040 mol sodium ethanoate, and 0.040 x 82 = 3.28 g.
9650 C is 0.1 F, and 4 F liberate 1 mol O2, so 0.025 mol O2 forms, which is 0.025 x 22.4 = 0.560 dm3.
In electrorefining, impure copper is made the anode so it dissolves and pure copper deposits on the cathode.
The hydride ion loses electrons, becoming H2, so it is oxidised and therefore acts as a reducing agent.
Products lie about 50 kJ/mol above reactants on the energy profile, so delta H is positive and equal to +50 kJ/mol.
Non-metal oxides that dissolve in water to form acids give solutions with pH less than 7.
In MnO4- manganese is +7, and in Mn2+ it is +2, so its oxidation number falls from +7 to +2.
The activation energy is the energy needed to reach the peak from the reactant level, which is peak y minus reactant level x.
For an exothermic reaction, raising the temperature shifts equilibrium backwards and lowers the equilibrium constant.
Heating ammonium nitrate decomposes it into dinitrogen oxide and steam.
Calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) is used up as HCl is added, so its concentration falls steadily to zero, shown by curve M.
Potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) reacting with concentrated HCl generates chlorine, which is then dried in the apparatus.
Iron does not react with alkaline solutions to release hydrogen, unlike aluminium, zinc and tin, which are amphoteric.
Residual chlorine from bleaching can react with and damage the fibres, so the clothes must be rinsed thoroughly.
Sulphate ions in sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI) form barium sulphate, a white precipitate that does not dissolve in acid.
The reaction of SO3 with water is violently exothermic and produces a mist, so SO3 is absorbed in concentrated acid instead.
Making iron the cathode in electrolysis prevents it from oxidising, so it is protected from corrosion.
Most metal oxides are basic, not acidic, so the statement that metal oxides are acidic is the false one.
Activity decreases in the order Na, Ca, Al, Fe, which follows the electrochemical series.
The compound has a triple bond at C1 and three methyl groups on C3, so it is 3,3-dimethylbut-1-yne.
Sodium reacts with ethanol to form sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas.
Alkanones are ketones, which have a carbonyl group bonded to two alkyl groups, giving the general formula R2CO.
Concentrated sulphuric acid protonates the ethanoate ion, releasing ethanoic acid.
48 g of carbon is 4 mol, and the molar mass is 2 x 28 = 56, so the formula is C4H8, which is an alkene.
Heating ethanol with a catalyst removes water from the molecule, so the reaction in flask G is dehydration.
Caustic soda absorbs the acidic sulphur(IV) oxide impurity formed during ethene preparation, leaving pure ethene.
In methane, carbon forms four equivalent bonds through sp3 hybridisation, mixing one 2s orbital and three 2p orbitals.
Bromine water is decolourised by C=C double bonds, so it confirms the presence of unsaturation.
